items.title: Roger Kellaway interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999
items.q: of course we had the old quartet which was Guerin, Tom Scott, Chuck Domanico and myself... So I became part of the L.A. Express. My only regret of that whole time is that out of 55 concerts, we recorded 9 times... Joe Sample wasn’t available for the tour

ctx.x: That’s great company. You’ve had kind of the cream on a lot of your projects. And you know it’s a long way from Anton Webern to Tom Scott and Joni Mitchell. You really kind of have this huge attention span and curiosity I guess.

Yeah that’s what it is, it is. It’s a curiosity. It’s an insatiable curiosity to understand how different ways of making music are achieved. So if you’re writing a comedy you do one thing, if you’re writing a horror picture you’re doing another thing and if it’s something that I’m asked to do that I’ve never done before I don’t say I can’t do that, I say I can do it, and I do my homework until I understand how it’s done, and then I go about doing it my way. But that’s the reason for all that. I love Joni…
